title: Sparse timeseries shingle mart for route forecasting
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Problem: Console needs a compact, query-friendly timeseries mart that supports short-horizon forecasting and anomaly detection for per-route and per-tenant traffic patterns. Current wide tables are expensive to query for moving-window models and produce high storage costs when keeping fine-grained per-invocation rows.

Proposal: Build a shingled timeseries mart that stores dense shingles (sliding windows) per route-tenant pair in a sparse, partitioned table. Each row represents a windowed feature vector (shingle) with metadata and pre-computed aggregates, optimized for ML training jobs and real-time forecasting lookups from the Console service.

Goals:
- Reduce query cost for moving-window feature extraction by >5x for common forecasting queries.
- Support lookback windows up to 7 days at sub-minute granularity (configurable).
- Provide canonicalized schema for both batch ML pipelines and fast ad-hoc analytics in Console dashboards.
- Maintain retention & compaction policy to balance storage and query performance.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Storing shingles increases write complexity and requires idempotent compaction jobs.
- Pre-aggregation may slightly delay freshness (targeting <90s end-to-end).
- Schema evolution for shingles must be controlled to avoid model training drift.

High level design:
1) Ingest: Stream invocation events into streaming tables (existing ingestion). A dedupe+enrichment job emits per-route-per-tenant minute-level aggregates.
2) Shingling job: Sliding window processor (Beam/Flink) converts minute aggregates into shingles (e.g., 60-min windows, stride 1 min). Each shingle row contains: route_id, tenant_id, window_start, window_end, features_shingle (array of numeric values serialized as BYTES), agg_features (scalar columns), event_counts, anomaly_score_placeholder, processing_ts.
3) Storage: BigQuery partitioned table (partitioned by window_date, clustered by tenant_id, route_id) with shingle payload stored in compressed BYTES and a compact JSON-ish schema string for quick sampling.
4) Materialization: Create a scheduled incremental materialized view (or a time-partitioned MV) that exposes decoded features as flattened columns for common queries and model backfills.
5) Consumption: ML pipelines consume shingles via the MV; Console alerting and forecasting services perform point lookups by (tenant_id, route_id, latest_window).

Operational concerns:
- Backfill strategy: use backfill job that replays dense minute aggregates into shingles, rate-limited.
- Idempotency: shingling job must write using deterministic keys (tenant_route_window) and safe upserts.
- Monitoring: track shingle generation lag, per-partition row skew, and MV refresh latency.
- Cost: estimate ~25% storage increase vs aggregated per-minute tables but >4x cost reduction on common ML query patterns.

Deliverables:
- Schema definition + example decoder UDFs for shingle BYTES -> FLOAT64[]
- Streaming shingler (Beam) with idempotent writes and integration tests
- Partitioned BigQuery table + MV templates + retention/compaction cron
- Migration runbook and rollback plan

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement the forecasting model itself, only the mart and access patterns required by forecast consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Shingled table schema committed to warehouse schema repo with decoder UDFs
Streaming shingler deployed to staging and producing shingles for a 72-hour window
Materialized view exposes flattened feature columns and can be queried in <1s for typical route lookups
End-to-end latency from event ingestion to shingle availability < 90s in staging
Backfill job can recreate 14 days of shingles and complete within agreed SLA
Monitoring dashboards for shingle lag, partition sizes, and MV refresh success exist and alert on SLO violations
implementation_notes: Use deterministic key (hash(tenant_id, route_id, window_start)) for upserts to make operations idempotent
Compress feature arrays using snappy + base64 for efficient BigQuery storage in BYTES
Cluster table by (tenant_id, route_id) to optimize point lookups for Console API
Leverage BigQuery MV for flattened hot-path queries; fall back to decoding functions when needed
Retention: keep raw shingles for 30 days, compact older windows to 1h resolution after 30 days
Estimate: streaming shingler CPU 4 vCPU per 5000 routes, test on staging with 20k routes
